questions.question: The loudness of sound is measured in which unit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decibel (dB)**__

 
• **Decibel (dB)** is the unit used to measure the loudness of sound.
 
• The decibel scale is a logarithmic scale that quantifies sound intensity.
 
• Sound levels are often measured in decibels using a sound level meter.
 
• The threshold of hearing is typically set at 0 dB, while sounds above 85 dB can potentially cause hearing damage over prolonged exposure.

 
• **Watt/sq. Metre (w/m2)** is a unit of sound intensity, not loudness.
 
• **Hertz (Hz)** measures the frequency of sound waves, not their loudness.
 
• **Sound intensity** is the power carried by sound waves per unit area in a direction perpendicular to that area, typically measured in watts per square meter.
 
• The decibel scale is used because the human ear perceives sound intensity logarithmically, meaning each 10 dB increase represents a tenfold increase in intensity.

questions.question: In which of the following states of India is the festival Bonalu celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Telangana**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bonalu** is a Hindu festival celebrated in the state of **Telangana**, India.
 
• The festival is dedicated to the Goddess Mahakali and is celebrated annually in the month of Ashada, which falls in July or August.
 
• During Bonalu, women prepare rice cooked with milk and jaggery in a new brass or earthen pot, adorned with neem leaves, turmeric, and vermilion. The pot is carried in a procession to the temple, accompanied by drum beats and dancing.
 
• The festival is considered a form of thanksgiving to the Goddess for fulfilling the devotees' vows.
 
• Bonalu is particularly popular in the twin cities of Hyderabad and Secunderabad, as well as other parts of Telangana.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The origin of Bonalu is believed to be linked to the plague epidemic that occurred in Hyderabad in 1813. People believed that the epidemic was a result of the anger of Goddess Mahakali, and they started offering Bonalu to appease her.
 
• The word 'Bonalu' is derived from the word 'Bhojanalu', which means meals or feast in Telugu, signifying the offering of food to the Goddess.
 
• Each temple in Telangana has its unique traditions and rituals associated with Bonalu, making the festival rich in cultural diversity.
 
• In addition to Bonalu, Telangana is also known for other festivals like Bathukamma, which is a floral festival celebrated by women.

questions.question: __________ partners with DAY-NULM towards empowering women entrepreneurs in June 2023.

• **UNDP** partnered with DAY-NULM in June 2023 to empower women entrepreneurs.
 
• DAY-NULM stands for **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Urban Livelihoods Mission**, which aims at reducing poverty and vulnerability of the urban poor households.

• **DAY-NULM** was launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation, Government of India, to uplift the urban poor by enhancing sustainable livelihood opportunities through skill development and access to credit.
 
• This partnership aims to integrate women into the economic mainstream by providing them with the necessary resources and support to start and grow their businesses.
 
• Such initiatives are vital for achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly those related to poverty reduction, gender equality, and economic growth.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the criteria to measure deprivations in the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 conducted by the government of India?

options.text: Households with no adult female aged 15-59
Households with only one room with no solid walls and roof
Households with no able bodied members

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Households with no adult female aged 15-59**__

__
 
• **Households with no adult female aged 15-59** is NOT one of the criteria to measure deprivations in the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011.
 
• The SECC 2011 used various criteria to measure deprivations including **households with differently-abled members**, **households with only one room with no solid walls and roof**, and **households with no able-bodied members**.
 
• The main objective of SECC 2011 was to identify households living with multiple deprivations and to provide a comprehensive picture of social and economic conditions in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011** was a landmark exercise conducted by the Government of India to gather comprehensive data on various socio-economic parameters.
 
• The SECC 2011 data was intended to be used for better targeting of government schemes and programs aimed at poverty alleviation and social welfare.
 
• The criteria used in SECC 2011 included parameters such as **households with no literate adult above 25 years**, **households with no adult male aged 15-59**, and **households with no adult female aged 15-59** was not one of them.
 
• The SECC 2011 was also aimed at capturing the socio-economic status of rural and urban households, enabling the identification of beneficiaries for various government schemes.

questions.question: After independence, India launched its First FYP in 1951, under _________ influence of first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After independence, India launched its First Five-Year Plan (FYP) in 1951 under the **socialist** influence of the first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• The plan was aimed at developing the agriculture sector, which was the backbone of the Indian economy at that time.
 
• It emphasized the role of the state in economic development and aimed to establish a mixed economy with both public and private sectors playing significant roles.
 
• The First FYP focused on land reforms, irrigation, and infrastructure development to boost agricultural productivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was greatly influenced by the socialist model of economic development, particularly the Soviet Union's centralized planning.
 
• The First FYP was prepared by the Planning Commission of India, which was established in 1950.
 
• The plan aimed at achieving a growth rate of 2.1% per annum in the national income.
 
• The success of the First FYP laid the foundation for subsequent plans and played a crucial role in shaping India's economic policies in the early years of independence.

questions.question: In India, subject to the provisions of article 333, the Legislative Assembly of each State shall consist of not more than __________ members.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**five hundred**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Constitution of India, the Legislative Assembly of each State shall consist of not more than **five hundred** members.
 
• This provision ensures that there is a limit to the number of representatives in the legislative assembly, promoting effective governance and management.
 
• Article 333 allows for the representation of the Anglo-Indian community in the legislative assemblies by nomination, if the President feels that the community is not adequately represented.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in Article 368.
 
• The Legislative Assembly serves as the lower house of the state legislature in India, with the Vidhan Parishad (Legislative Council) serving as the upper house in some states.

questions.question: In which year was the Treaty of Amritsar signed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1809**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1809** is the year in which the Treaty of Amritsar was signed.
 
• The Treaty of Amritsar was an agreement between the British East India Company and Maharaja Ranjit Singh of the Sikh Empire.
 
• It was signed on **25th March 1809**.
 
• The treaty established the Sutlej River as the boundary between the Sikh Empire and the British territories in India.
 
• This agreement helped in maintaining peace between the two powers and allowed the British to focus on their other territorial interests in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maharaja Ranjit Singh** was the founder of the Sikh Empire in the northwest Indian subcontinent in the early half of the 19th century.
 
• The **British East India Company** was a British trading company that eventually came to rule large areas of India, exercising military and administrative control.
 
• The Treaty of Amritsar is a significant event in Indian history as it marked the beginning of formal relations between the British and the Sikh Empire.
 
• This treaty allowed the British to further consolidate their power in India by securing their northern frontier.
 
• The treaty also ensured that the British would not interfere in the internal matters of the Sikh Empire.

• **Kathakali** is a classical dance form from Kerala, known for its elaborate costumes and makeup.
 
• Kathak dance performances often include a mix of storytelling, rhythmic foot movements, and facial expressions.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the second Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lt General Anil Chauhan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lt General Anil Chauhan** has been appointed as the second Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) in India.
 
• The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) is a high-ranking military officer who serves as the principal military advisor to the Minister of Defence and heads the Department of Military Affairs.
 
• The position was created to bring better coordination and integration among the three branches of the Indian Armed Forces: the Army, Navy, and Air Force.
 
• Lt General Anil Chauhan succeeded General Bipin Rawat, the first CDS of India, who tragically passed away in a helicopter crash.
 
• The appointment of the CDS is part of ongoing military reforms aimed at enhancing the operational capabilities and effectiveness of the Indian Armed Forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) also chairs the Chiefs of Staff Committee, which includes the heads of the Army, Navy, and Air Force.
 
• The CDS is responsible for facilitating joint operations, procurement, and training among the three services.
 
• This role is crucial for ensuring a unified strategic direction and integrated approach to national security.
 
• The creation of the CDS position was recommended by various committees and experts over the years to improve the synergy and efficiency of the Indian military.
 
• Lt General Anil Chauhan has had a distinguished military career, holding various command and staff positions before being appointed as the CDS.

questions.question: A _________ tank called the NITI Aayog was established to advise the government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**policy think**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NITI Aayog** is a policy think tank of the Government of India, established with the aim to foster cooperative federalism by involving the states in the decision-making process.
 
• It was formed on **1st January 2015**, replacing the Planning Commission which followed a top-down model.
 
• The full form of NITI Aayog is **National Institution for Transforming India**.
 
• NITI Aayog provides strategic and technical advice across various sectors to the central and state governments.
 
• Its initiatives include promoting sustainable development, fostering innovation, and enhancing economic policy planning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Planning Commission** was established in 1950 and functioned for over six decades until it was replaced by NITI Aayog.
 
• NITI Aayog's governing council includes all **Chief Ministers** of states and **Lieutenant Governors** of Union Territories, reflecting its inclusive approach.
 
• It emphasizes on a bottom-up approach to planning, ensuring that regional needs and aspirations are considered in national policy formulation.
 
• NITI Aayog also focuses on monitoring and evaluating the implementation of government programs and initiatives.
 
• Its key areas of focus include health, education, agriculture, and infrastructure development.

questions.question: As per Census-2011, Which of the following states have the highest female literacy rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kerala** has the highest female literacy rate among Indian states as per Census 2011.
 
• The female literacy rate in Kerala is **92.07%**.
 
• This high literacy rate is attributed to Kerala's strong emphasis on education and social reforms.
 
• Kerala's literacy programs have focused on improving educational access for women and marginalized communities.
 
• The state's robust public education system and progressive policies have played a significant role in achieving this milestone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census 2011** is the 15th National Census survey conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India.
 
• It provides comprehensive data on various demographic, social, and economic parameters.
 
• The literacy rate is defined as the percentage of literate people aged seven years and above.
 
• Kerala has consistently maintained a high literacy rate, both for males and females, due to its effective educational policies.
 
• The state's focus on universal primary education and adult literacy programs has significantly contributed to its high literacy rates.
